svg.text: Every minute, a truck full of plastic waste ends up in the world's oceans. Most of it
comes from land: plastic bottles, bags and packaging that are thrown away carelessly
or carried to the sea by rivers.
The consequences are terrible. Turtles mistake plastic bags for jellyfish and die
after eating them, while seabirds feed their chicks pieces of plastic by accident. In
addition, large plastic items slowly break into tiny particles, which fish swallow.
Fortunately, there are things we can do. Some countries have banned free plastic bags,
and the number of bags used has fallen by more than 80%. Many cities have started to
clean their beaches regularly, and several companies now make clothes and shoes from
However, experts warn that these efforts are not enough unless people change their
